clue.text: Forbidden City artist's a blank slate

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
LA is Los Angeles, the city
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist, plus the 's

explanation.surface: An artist from Beijing's Forbidden City turns out to have nothing on their canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidden City' looks like one place, but it splits into 'forbidden' and 'City'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names a mind not yet written on, literally a scraped tablet with nothing on it.

clue.text: Defame American beginning to dither during ceasefire

indicators.note: the American and the opening of dither come during, so inside, the ceasefire word

parts.note: a truce is a ceasefire

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of dither

explanation.surface: An American hesitates while a ceasefire holds, and is slandered for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to slander or malign them, damaging their reputation.

clue.text: Freezing cold bum pinched by two brothers? Yes, in play

indicators.note: something pinched by two things is gripped between them, so the bum sits between the brothers

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for brother
a monk is a brother of a religious order
ass is American slang for the bottom

indicators.note: letters in play are moving about, so the word yes is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky stage romp in which two brothers pinch a frozen backside and cry yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges YES into EYS. The phrase 'cold enough to freeze the balls off a brass monkey' is British slang for bitter cold.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal idiom for bitterly chilly weather, short for a cold that would affect a brass monkey.

clue.text: Can one going there be said to be more idiotic?

indicators.note: said tells us the words are spoken, and we listen to how they sound

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet (loo), and one going there to urinate is a peer, someone who pees

explanation.surface: A daft riddle asking whether a person visiting the toilet counts as sillier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' is the childish sense of relieving oneself, so the one going in the can is a 'loo peer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for crazy or daft, and the comparative form means sillier still.

clue.text: Tasty bit of flesh enthrals a couple of males in Turkish bath

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the meat holds the other letters inside

parts.note: ham is a tasty cut of pork
M is the abbreviation for male, so two give MM

explanation.surface: A sensual scene of a tasty-looking body captivating a pair of men in a steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabic-derived word names a Middle Eastern steam bath, the kind often called Turkish.

clue.text: Add gaseous mixture to a tea drunk by the Queen

indicators.note: by here places the Queen alongside and within the rearranged tea letters
drunk means disordered, so the letters of a tea are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Instructions to fizz up a cup of tea that the Queen is drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like the Queen sipping, but it signals the rearrangement; 'by' then sets her royal cipher among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerating something introduces air, the gaseous mixture we breathe, into a liquid or soil.

clue.text: Fat spillage? Bungle and point rudely

parts.note: to muff something is to bungle it

indicators.note: rudely means roughly or crudely, so the letters of point are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fumbling an awkward moment and then jabbing a finger at a person's waistline.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for a roll of belly fat bulging over a tight waistband like a cake over its case.

clue.text: See 2
When stranded, how's your father to get a cocktail?

parts.note: British slang euphemism for sexual intercourse
a sailor stranded ashore, out of work, is said to be on the beach

explanation.surface: Someone shipwrecked ashore seeking a drink, with a cheeky British euphemism thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's your father' is old British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Named mixed drink of vodka, peach schnapps and fruit juices, popular in bars since the 1980s.

clue.text: See 1
Go too far in clarifying heartless rule in case of one fiver being lost

indicators.note: something put in the case of other letters is enclosed by them
being lost suggests the letters have wandered into a new order
removing the heart of the word rule leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A legal quibble about a rule concerning a lost five-pound note, argued too fussily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being lost' signals the rearrangement of the money words; 'heartless' empties the rule, and 'in case of' encloses what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine excessively is to purify or polish something beyond the useful point.

clue.text: Breakfast food starts to make us evacuate (some linseed involved)

indicators.note: the starts of the following six words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A warning that a high-fibre breakfast, with linseed in it, will send us to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit, eaten in the morning with milk.

clue.text: Got ring? Badly in debt again, at first

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly, so rearranged
at first takes the opening letter of again

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a ring was bought, having slipped into debt once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: to have acquired something is to have got it.

clue.text: Bore through getting to speak at length about France

indicators.note: the speaking word goes about, around, the letter for France

parts.note: to perorate is to speak at length, or sum up a speech
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A dull speaker droning on about France becomes a bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' pretends to be a tedious person, but it is the verb to drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or drill holes through a surface, making it full of punctures.

clue.text: Entertaining lady with extremely neat backside

parts.note: something entertaining is fun
a dame is a lady, also a titled woman

indicators.note: the extremes of the word neat are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cheeky comic lady with a remarkably shapely rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like a verb taking the lady, but it is just the word fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal and humorous term for the buttocks or anus, the body's bottom.

clue.text: Lift people out of morass? I took over

indicators.note: turned over means read in the opposite direction
out of says the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Rescuers haul people from a bog, and someone claims to have taken charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SITO, found inside 'morass? I took', back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Otis Elevator Company is the famous maker of lifts, so its people are the lift firm.

clue.text: Person getting kiss from Douglas?

parts.note: man is a person, or humankind
X is the sign for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone receives a kiss from a man named Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is a man's name in the surface, but it is the capital of the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, so anything from there is of that island.

clue.text: Scottish island with one foreign plant

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A Hebridean island with one exotic plant growing on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall woolly-leaved herb with yellow flower spikes, a wild flowering plant of Europe.

clue.text: Minerals lads regularly put in iron boxes

indicators.note: the chosen letters are put in between the other pieces

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
spars is boxes in the sense of sparring, fighting practice bouts

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one of lads

explanation.surface: Some lads are locked away in iron containers with mineral samples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like containers but is the verb: spars.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of rock-forming silicate minerals, the most abundant in the Earth's crust.

clue.text: Decline to remove odour?

definitions.meaning: a decline or fall is a going down
read as de- plus scent, to take the smell away, a whimsical coinage

explanation.surface: Refusing to take away a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or a fall in fortune, both senses of decline.

clue.text: Given stripe in primary colour, as curtains may be

indicators.note: the stripe goes in the colour word

parts.note: red is one of the primary colours
a line is a stripe

explanation.surface: Fabric given a stripe in red, as curtains sometimes are.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains are often lined, and old curtains may be given a new backing fabric.

clue.text: Creator of Fantasy Island comic, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: Malta is a Mediterranean island
comic means funny, witty

explanation.surface: Suggests the person who devised a TV show called Fantasy Island, joking about its host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantasy Island' looks like the TV show, but Island is the wordplay. Swapping M and W in Malta witty gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thurber's daydreaming hero is a byword for someone who invents fantasies about himself.

clue.text: Almost go in prison in Split, due to bust?

indicators.note: the shortened verb goes in the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a prison

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A prisoner escapes jail after breaking out in a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a Croatian city or a jailbreak, but it is the dividing line between breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible separation between a woman's breasts, a split caused by the bust.

clue.text: Fools one politician hired, working on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the pieces go inside the steamship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is on board
I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
let means rented out, hired
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: Idiots, including one politician taken on to work aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: a simpleton is a foolish, gullible person.

clue.text: See 20
Mushroom terrine starter coated with syrup, after top taken off container

indicators.note: the inner pieces are coated with, enclosed by, the syrup word
the top of the word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: treacle is a dark syrup
a cep is a porcini mushroom

indicators.note: the starter of terrine is its first letter

explanation.surface: A recipe for a mushroom terrine glazed with syrup, the lid then removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any vessel or holder made to receive something.

clue.text: See 22
Kind of brown-backed flower

indicators.note: backed means moved back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: tan is a light brown
in crosswords a flower is a river, something that flows; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A type of flower whose back is brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (the Ure, in Yorkshire), not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and nature both mean the type or essential character of something.

clue.text: Remained sober, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so we go by sound

parts.note: staid means sober and sedate

explanation.surface: Someone who kept off the drink, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: to have stayed is to have remained in place.
